name: Shashak
overview: Shashak is a male figure from the tribe of Benjamin, uniquely identified as the son of Elpaal according to 1 Chronicles 8:14. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes provided.
namesAndTitles: The single recorded name is Shashak, which is a proper name noted in 1 Chronicles 8:14. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is given in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shashak as the son of Elpaal. Additionally, several inferred paternal relationships are noted in the same genealogical context, connecting him to ancestors such as Ishpan, Eber, Eliel, Abdon, Zichri, Hanan, Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah, Iphdeiah, and Penuel, all within the tribe of Benjamin.
scriptureSignificance: Shashak's significance lies in his place within the genealogical record of the tribe of Benjamin, demonstrating the faithfulness of God in preserving the lineage of His people. His mention underscores the importance of family heritage and tribal identity in the biblical narrative, serving as a link in the ancestral line that reflects God's providential care over Israel.
